questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

Jaya asked Sushmita to reminds her about the meeting.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1.**

The error lies in the 2nd part of the sentence.

As per the Subject-Verb agreement rule, The verb must agree with its Subject in Number and person. Sushmita being the 2nd person must agree with 2nd person singular verb.

Thus, **'Reminds'** should be replaced with **'remind'.**

__The infinitive is the base of the of a verb which is often preceded by 'to'.__

Thus the correct sentence will be: *Jaya asked Sushmita to remind her about the meeting.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

Rashmi is not only smart __but very beautiful.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**but also very beautiful**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The conjunction pair is not only...but also__.
 
• Correlative conjunctions always come in pairs and they relate one part of the sentence to the other. "Not only... but also" can be used to connect either nouns or clauses. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Using *not only . . . but also***** in a sentence**, **parallelism**** should be the goal**. It means that the words following both parts of this correlative conjunction (i.e., *not only* and *but also*) should belong to the same parts of speech. For example, if a verb follows *not only*, then a verb should also follow *but also*. Using different parts of speech after each part of *not only . . . but also* makes the sentence imbalanced and, frankly, just awkward. 

 **Example: **He’s not only intelligent but also has a great sense of humor.

 He’s not only intelligent but also funny.

 

**Thus the correct sentence will be:** *Rashmi is not only smart but also very beautiful.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

I'll be at the parlour __near 5 P.M.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**till'.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition '**near'** means '**not far away in distance**'. 

 
 
• **Example**: My mother loves to sit **near **the lamp.
 
 
 
• **'Along'** is a preposition used to denote **position on a line**.
 
 
• **Example**: There was a thick line of trees **along** the road. 
 
 
 
• **'Unless'** is a conjunction which means '**except if**'
 
 
• **Example**: They won't come unless you invite them. 
 
 
 
• **'Till'** is a preposition that means **'up to the time of'**.
 
 
• **Example**: He waited** till **3 O'clock. 
 
 
 
• **'Unless'** is action-oriented conjunction hence, can't be used with time. 
 
• The usage of the other options thus makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.

 

**The correct sentence is:** I'll be at the parlour till 5 P.M.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/efb90c3647c276e117dc17fb6439410dad00fafe8f511a89c38f32cba7de65df.png] 

 
• In the given sentence,** 5 P.M.** signifies that a **preposition of time** should be used. This will help us to eliminate the two options- '**along'** and** 'near'** as they are prepositions of place.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Preposition of time**: at, since, ago, during, till, until, before, after.
 
• 
 **Preposition of direction**: above, across, along, below, behind, over.
 
 
• **Preposition of place**: In, at upon, beside, under, from, on.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

If I had known about him before I will have recommended him.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **‘I will have**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence starts with **‘If’. **‘If’ denotes that the question is a **conditional sentence** and more accurately, it is an example of** third conditional sentence**.
 
• Third conditional sentence is used to explain that present situation would be different if something different had happened in the past.
 
• The incident that happens first or was supposed to happen first takes a past perfect tense **(had + V3 form of verb)** in the ‘If’ clause when **‘would/should/could have’ **is present in the main clause that expresses the hypothetical situation that could have happened.
 
• In the question, ‘If I had known about him before’ is the incident that is supposed to happen first. Therefore, ‘would have recommended’ (had + V3 form of verb) should be the correct verb form used here.

Therefore, the corrected sentence is: "*If I had known about him before, I **would have **recommended him."*

questions.question: If A = 1 and ANT = 105 then ASK = ?
questions.solution:
The logic is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/138e28aa5b9f952177eafcbbd33d71c858c75fb3e3ca41bf7c93847a9e6ebf5f.png] 

A = 1

ANT → A = 1, N = 14, T = 20

A + N + T = 1 + 14 + 20 = 35

35 × 3 = 105

Thus, ANT = 105

Similarly,

ASK → A = 1, S = 19, K = 11

A + S + K = 1 + 19 + 11 = 31

31 × 3 = 93

So, ASK = 93

Hence, ‘93’ is the correct answer.

**Statement:**

I. All ﬂowers are trees.

II. All trees are fruits.

Conclusions:

I. Some fruits are ﬂowers.

 II. All ﬂowers are fruits.

options.text: Either conclusion I or II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

 II. All ﬂowers are fruits. → True

questions.question:

**Statements:**

A. Some drivers are racers.

B. Some racers are pilots.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some pilots are drivers.

II. No pilot is a driver

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Either conclusion I or II follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cfc96e4dffdfadd1b53187ee1542413db403c1f14dc562e9a810f0f7dc31146f.png]

But, conclusion I and II forms a complementary pair.

Hence, either conclusion I or II follows.

questions.question: A is taller than F, who is shorter than three persons. C is shorter than D, who is the tallest. B is taller than E. C is neither shorter than F nor taller than A. Who is the second shortest person among the given?

questions.question: Pipes A and B can empty a full tank in 8 and 12 hours, respectively. C is a filling pipe. All the three pipes were opened together at the same time and one-sixth of the tank got emptied in one hour. C alone can fill the tank in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipes A and B can empty a full tank in 8 and 12 hours, respectively.

C is a filling pipe.

All the three pipes were opened together at the same time and one-sixth of the tank got emptied in one hour.

**Formula:**

If a pipe empties a tank in 'a' hours and an another empties the same tank in 'b' hours then

Total work = LCM of the times taken by two different pipes = LCM of (a, b)

Efficiency of first pipe = (-) LCM of (a, b)/a

Efficiency of second pipe = (-) LCM of (a, b)/b

Time taken to fill the tank = Total work/The combined efficiency of the pipes.

Now, if another pipe fills the tank in 'c' hours, then

Combined efficiency of the three pipes = (- efficiency of pipe A) + (- efficiency of pipe B) + (+ efficiency of pipe C)

(-)ve sign is mentioned as they empty the tank and (+)ve sign is to imply that the pipe fills the tank.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/716db7cfaeda1353ddfb5f5d9a747cb22febeba60c0c3f5c1f3475bcc2842393.png] 

Here in the fig, LCM of (8, 12) = 24 = Total work 

Efficiency of A = 24/8 = 3

Efficiency of B = 24/12 = 2

(-)ve sign is mentioned as A and B empty the tank.

1/6th of total work = 24/6 = 4 = combined efficiency of three pipes

Let the efficiency of pipe C be x, then

⇒ x – 3 – 2 = – 4

⇒ x = 5 – 4

⇒ x = 1

**∴ the pipe C alone can fill the tank in = 24/1 = 24 hrs**

questions.question: The average of 21 numbers is 44. The average of the first 11 numbers is 48 and that of the last 11 numbers is 42. If the 11th number is excluded, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.solution:

Sum of 21 numbers = 44 × 21 = 924

The average of the first 11 numbers = 48

The sum of the first 11 numbers = 48 × 11 = 528

The average of the last 11 numbers = 42

The sum of the last 11 numbers = 42 × 11 = 462

11th number = 462 + 528 – 924 = 66

The sum of 20 numbers = 924 – 66 = 858

Average of 20 numbers = 858/20 = 42.9

questions.question: The total surface area of a solid cylinder is 1155 cm². Its curved surface area is two-fifth of its total surface area. What is the height (in cm) of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
As we know,

Curved surface area of cylinder = 2 πrh

Total surface area of the cylinder = 2 πr (r + h)

According to the question

2πrh = (2/5) × 2πr (r + h)

⇒ 5h = 2r + 2h

⇒ 5h – 2h = 2r

⇒ 3h = 2r

Let r : h = 3x : 2x

Total surface area of the cylinder = 2 πr (r + h)

2 πr (r + h) = 1155

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 3x (3x + 2x) = 1155

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 3x × 5x = 1155

⇒ x² = (1155 × 7)/(2 × 22 × 3 × 5) = (7 × 7)/(2 × 2)

⇒ x = √[(7 × 7)/(2 × 2)]

⇒ x = 7/2

Height of the cylinder = 2 × (7/2) = 7 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.**

questions.question: What 5,6,8,9 and 12 divide the least number x, the remainder each case is 1, but x is divisible by 13. What will be the remainder when x is divided by 31?

(360x + 1)/13

(9x + 1) is divisible by 13 if we put x = 1, 2, 3, 4, ……..

Put x = 10, then

⇒ (9 × 10 + 1)

⇒ 91

As we know, 91 is divisible by 13 so put x = 10

360x + 1

⇒ 360 × 10 + 1

⇒ 3600 + 1

⇒ 3601

If 3601 is divisible by 31, the the remainder will be 5.

questions.question: ________ is considered as the oldest discovered Indus Valley Civilization site.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhirrana.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhirrana**__ is considered the oldest discovered Indus Valley Civilization site.
 
• It is the oldest one according to the C-14 radio-dating done by the Archaeological Survey of India.
 
• It is situated in the Fatehabad district and dates to 757-6200 BC.
 
• Rakhigarhi, situated close to Bhirrama is the largest Harappan site in the world.
 
• Mohenjo-Daro is situated in southern Pakistan.
 
• Allahdino is located towards each of Karachi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Indus Valley Civilization was spread from present-day North-East Afghanistan to Pakistan and North-West India. This civilization flourished in the river basins of the Ghaggar-Hakra river and the Indus. Indus valley civilization is one of the four oldest civilizations in the world. It is also known as Harappan Civilization and is well-known for its organized planning based on the grid system. Important facts to be remembered 
 
• John Marshall was the first researcher to use the term, ‘Indus Valley Civilization’.
 
• Indus Valley Civilization spread from the year 2500 – 1750 BC according to radio-carbon dating.
 
• The most distinctive feature of the Harappan Civilization was its urbanization.
 
• Moreover, sheep and goats, dogs, humped cattle buffalo, and elephants were domesticated in the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The capital cities are Mohenjodaro and Harappa.
 
• The port cities are Sutkagendor, Balakot, Lothal, Allahdino, and Kuntasi.
 
• The Indus valley people were well-acquainted with the use of both cotton and wool.
 
• Name of the major cities are given below:
 
 
• Mohenjodaro (Sind)-It is located on the right bank of the Indus.
 
• Kalibangan (Rajasthan)-It was on the banks of the river Ghaggar river
 
• Chanhudaro-It lies on the left bank of the Indus in the south of Mohenjodaro.
 
• Lothal- It is located at the head of the Gulf of Cambay.
 
• Surkotada (Gujarat)-It is at the head of the Rann of Kutch.
 
• Banawali (Haryana)-It was situated on the banks of the now-extinct Sarasvati
 
• Dholavira (Gujarat)-It excavated is in the Kutch district

questions.question: Car moving on a straight road is an example of ________ motion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rectilinear**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Point__**

__
 
• Car moving on a straight road is an example of **rectilinear**__ motion.
 
• When two particles of a body travel same distance along 2 parallel straight lines then that is known as Rectilinear motion or straight-line motion.
 
• Periodic motion is that which is repeated in equal intervals of time.
 
• Curvilinear motion is that which occurs when a particle travels along a curved path.
 
• Random motion is an unpredictable motion in which the object moves in a random direction.
